module_title: Recognising Red Flags in Parenting & Family Dynamics
learning_outcomes: Identify early red flags in parent–child interactions.
Recognise behavioural, emotional, and relational warning signs.
Understand how red flags signal deeper patterns of harm or instability.
Interpret red flags in co-parenting, household dynamics, and child behaviour.
Apply safe, supportive responses when red flags appear.

lesson_content.definition: Red flags are early indicators of harmful patterns in parenting, family dynamics, or child wellbeing. They are patterns, not isolated moments.

categories.name: Parent–Child Interaction Red Flags
examples: Child becomes hyper-vigilant around parent's mood
Parent uses fear, shame, or humiliation to gain compliance
Child stops expressing emotions to avoid conflict
Parent dismisses or mocks child's feelings

categories.name: Co-Parenting Red Flags
examples: One parent undermines the other's decisions
Child used as messenger or emotional support
Isolation from the other parent or extended family
Child expresses fear about transitions between homes

categories.name: Household Dynamic Red Flags
examples: One person dominates decisions or routines

categories.name: Child Behaviour Red Flags
examples: Strong reactions to tone or facial expressions
Sleep difficulties or unexplained physical complaints

categories.name: Parent Internal Experience Red Flags
examples: Feeling confused about what is real

video_lesson.title: Recognising Red Flags Early
script: Red flags are early signals that something in the family system is creating fear, instability, or emotional harm.
They often appear subtly, through patterns of behaviour rather than single incidents.
Recognising red flags early helps parents respond with clarity and protect emotional safety.
This lesson explores red flags across parent–child interactions, co-parenting, household dynamics, and child behaviour.
